senses.definition: excessive admiration or praise
senses.example: The young actor found the adulation of his fans hard to live up to.

senses.definition: comparable in certain respects, so that a comparison can be drawn
senses.example: The heart is analogous to a pump.

senses.definition: to calm or satisfy someone by giving in to their demands
senses.example: The company appeased angry customers with a full refund.

senses.definition: to support or strengthen
senses.example: New evidence bolstered the case for the defense.

senses.definition: concise and exact use of words
senses.example: The editor praised the brevity of her report.

senses.definition: shortness of time
senses.example: The brevity of their visit disappointed the grandparents.

senses.definition: clear, logical and convincing
senses.example: She made a cogent case for delaying the launch.

senses.definition: to accept or allow behavior that is considered wrong
senses.example: The school does not condone cheating of any kind.

senses.definition: behavior that follows accepted standards or rules
senses.example: The novel is a protest against the conformity of suburban life.

senses.definition: standing out so as to be clearly visible; attracting notice
senses.example: Her red coat was conspicuous in the sea of gray suits.

senses.definition: feeling or expressing remorse at the recognition that one has done wrong
senses.example: The contrite driver apologized to the family again and again.

senses.definition: extremely complex and difficult to follow
senses.example: The film's convoluted plot left most of the audience confused.

senses.definition: to discourage someone from doing something by instilling doubt or fear
senses.example: Higher fines are meant to deter people from littering.

senses.definition: disagreement between people
senses.example: Money was a constant source of discord in the family.

senses.definition: to draw out a response, answer or fact from someone
senses.example: The question elicited a long silence.

words.note: Elicit means to draw out; illicit means illegal.

senses.definition: to make something more attractive by adding details or decorations
senses.example: The jacket was embellished with silver embroidery.

senses.definition: to make a story more interesting by adding details that are often untrue
senses.example: He tends to embellish his fishing stories.

senses.definition: based on observation or experience rather than theory or pure logic
senses.example: There is little empirical evidence for the claim.

senses.definition: lasting for a very short time
senses.example: Fame on social media is often ephemeral.

senses.definition: a speech or piece of writing that praises someone highly, typically someone who has just died
senses.example: Her son gave a moving eulogy at the funeral.

senses.definition: serving as a desirable model; very good
senses.example: The nurse was praised for her exemplary care.

senses.definition: (of a punishment) serving as a warning
senses.example: The judge handed down an exemplary sentence to deter others.

senses.definition: uncalled for; lacking good reason
senses.example: Critics objected to the film's gratuitous violence.

senses.definition: given or done free of charge
senses.example: The guide offered gratuitous advice to every tourist he met.

senses.definition: arrogantly superior and disdainful
senses.example: The haughty waiter sniffed at our choice of wine.

senses.definition: of the same kind; alike
senses.example: The suburb's houses were homogeneous, each a copy of the next.

senses.definition: a person who attacks cherished beliefs or institutions
senses.example: An iconoclast in her field, she challenged decades of accepted theory.

senses.definition: a mode of behavior or way of thought peculiar to an individual
senses.example: One of his idiosyncrasies was eating dessert first.

senses.definition: implied though not plainly expressed
senses.example: There was an implicit threat in his offer.

senses.definition: with no qualification or question; absolute
senses.example: She had implicit trust in her doctor.

senses.definition: continuing without pause or interruption
senses.example: The incessant rain flooded the low fields.

senses.definition: unwilling or refusing to change one's views or to agree about something
senses.example: Talks failed because both sides remained intransigent.

senses.definition: having or showing a tendency to be easily angered
senses.example: The irascible old chef shouted at anyone who touched his knives.

senses.definition: using very few words
senses.example: His laconic reply, "No," ended the discussion.

senses.definition: to make something bad less severe, serious or painful
senses.example: Planting trees can mitigate the effects of flooding.

words.note: Mitigate means to lessen; militate means to be a powerful factor against something.

senses.definition: to appease the anger or anxiety of someone
senses.example: The manager mollified the angry customer with a free meal.

senses.definition: lacking interest or excitement; dull
senses.example: Most of the job is mundane paperwork.

senses.definition: of this earthly world rather than a heavenly or spiritual one
senses.example: The monks set aside mundane concerns.

senses.definition: designed to impress or attract notice; showy
senses.example: Their ostentatious wedding had fireworks and a string orchestra.

senses.definition: having an unemotional and stolidly calm disposition
senses.example: The phlegmatic pilot calmly announced that one engine had failed.

senses.definition: seeming reasonable or probable
senses.example: Her explanation for being late was plausible.

senses.definition: to divide or cause to divide into two sharply contrasting groups
senses.example: The proposal polarized the town into supporters and opponents.

senses.definition: (of a child) having developed certain abilities at an earlier age than usual
senses.example: The precocious girl was reading novels at five.

senses.definition: having or showing knowledge of events before they take place
senses.example: Her prescient warning about the housing bubble was ignored.

senses.definition: in its original condition; unspoiled
senses.example: The old car was in pristine condition.

senses.definition: lacking poetic beauty; commonplace or dull
senses.example: The truth was more prosaic: the ghost was a loose shutter.

senses.definition: (of something unwelcome) flourishing or spreading unchecked
senses.example: Corruption was rampant in the old regime.

senses.definition: having an obstinately uncooperative attitude toward authority or discipline
senses.example: The teacher kept the recalcitrant pupils after class.

senses.definition: extremely thorough and careful
senses.example: The drug went through rigorous testing.

senses.definition: (of a rule or system) strictly applied or adhered to
senses.example: The academy is known for its rigorous discipline.

senses.definition: so delicate or precise as to be difficult to analyze or describe
senses.example: There is a subtle difference between the two shades of blue.

senses.definition: making use of clever and indirect methods to achieve something
senses.example: He dropped a subtle hint that he wanted to leave.

senses.definition: diverging from a previous course; peripheral
senses.example: His point was tangential to the main discussion.

senses.definition: a long, angry speech of criticism or accusation
senses.example: He launched into a tirade about the state of the trains.

senses.definition: easy to control or influence
senses.example: The horse was more tractable after a week of training.

senses.definition: (of a problem) easy to deal with
senses.example: Breaking the project into steps made it more tractable.

senses.definition: using or expressed in more words than are needed
senses.example: The verbose report could have been a single page.

senses.definition: capable of working successfully; feasible
senses.example: Solar power is now a viable alternative to coal.

senses.definition: feeling or showing caution about possible dangers or problems
senses.example: Be wary of offers that seem too good to be true.
